text:
Whether to rent or buy depends less on ideology than on how long you plan to stay. Buying costs 2–5% of the purchase price in closing costs, plus agent commissions when you resell. If you expect to move within roughly five years, you usually lose money. Early mortgage payments go mostly to interest, and equity builds very slowly.

The price-to-rent ratio of a market gives a useful hint. Above about 20, renting is favored. Below 15, buying is favored.

First-time buyers often stretch to take the largest loan a lender will approve. Many then find that owning has its own steady costs: maintenance alone takes 1–2% of the home's value each year. A 20% down payment avoids private mortgage insurance.

Run a rent-versus-own calculator, then check its results against how likely you are to change jobs and move. Treat the house as shelter first and an investment second: the roof matters more than the return. Renters who diligently invest the money they save often match the net worth of owners.
